dependsOn: DAS — Data Access Service (social compliance config)
EntitlementService — user role and permission store

gapAnalysis.title: CMS is the authoritative persistence layer — channel-service owns no data
gapAnalysis.detail: Every aggregate (Channel, Post, Comment, Announcement, Social*) persists exclusively via CMSServiceProvider HTTP calls. The channel-service domain model cannot enforce cross-aggregate invariants, cannot run atomic transactions, and is entirely unavailable if CMS is down. The domain layer is a pure orchestration shell, not an authoritative store. This is the foundational architectural risk.

gapAnalysis.title: Infrastructure proxies exposed as domain controllers
gapAnalysis.detail: DASController/DASAppService, FMSController/FMSAppService, EntitlementController/EntitlementAppService, and BlobStorageController/BSSAppService are pure pass-through proxies with no owned aggregate, no business logic, and no lifecycle. They expose external service APIs directly on the channel-service's API surface, creating tight coupling between API consumers and the internals of downstream services. These should be encapsulated behind internal anti-corruption layer (ACL) adapters and not surfaced as independent controllers.

gapAnalysis.title: Compliance data structures duplicated across Social domains
gapAnalysis.detail: SocialContentEntity and SocialShareEntity both carry full inline compliance response objects (ContentResponse, Violation, Evidence, ContentCategory hierarchies) — identical structures duplicated verbatim across both entities. A Compliance value object should be extracted and shared, or a dedicated Compliance aggregate in the SocialCompliance domain should own this data and expose a reference from the other aggregates.

gapAnalysis.title: PostEntity carries denormalized ChannelName
gapAnalysis.detail: PostEntity.ChannelName is a denormalized cross-domain field with an inline TODO comment: 'temporary fix until we can get the channel details from the post' (SP-10102). This violates aggregate boundary rules — Post should never store Channel data. Channel details should be resolved at query time via the Channel domain service rather than embedded in the Post aggregate.

gapAnalysis.title: Attachment refill logic duplicated across four aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: PostEntity, CommentEntity, SocialContentEntity, and SocialShareEntity all implement identical AddAttachment() and Refill() methods (~200 lines) for LibraryContent, ProfileContent, WorkSpaceContent, and PeerToPeerContent. This pattern is copy-pasted four times. It should be extracted into a ContentAttachmentCollection value object or a ContentRefillService domain service to eliminate duplication and centralize invariant enforcement.

gapAnalysis.title: UserDetailsEntity parses JObject in domain constructor
gapAnalysis.detail: UserDetailsEntity's constructor accepts a raw JObject and performs JSON deserialization (preferenceDetailsToken.ToObject<UserPreferenceDetailsEntity>()) to populate sub-entities. JSON parsing is an infrastructure concern that must not appear in domain entities. The repository or mapper layer should deserialize the JSON into typed DTOs before passing them to the entity constructor.

gapAnalysis.title: Task.Run cache invalidation fired directly in controllers
gapAnalysis.detail: PostController.CreateOrUpdatePostAsync and AnnouncementController.CreateAnnouncementAsync use Task.Run() to trigger cache reloads without awaiting. These fire-and-forget calls will silently fail, are untestable, and bypass the application service contract. Cache invalidation should be expressed as a domain event consumed by a dedicated handler.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events for this service's own aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: VideoProcessedEvent exists only for inbound Kafka consumption. The channel-service emits zero domain events for its own state changes (ChannelCreated, PostPublished, CommentCreated, etc.). All cross-domain side-effects (cache, notifications, downstream updates) are wired as direct synchronous calls in AppService or controllers, making the model non-evolvable and tightly coupled.

gapAnalysis.title: Content Access controllers are proxy anti-pattern
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentController, FMSController, DASController, and BlobStorageController expose external-service APIs through the channel-service API surface without adding any domain logic. This creates implicit coupling: callers treating channel-service as a gateway to CMS/FMS/DAS will break when those contracts change. These should be consolidated into a declared ACL adapter or removed.

gapAnalysis.title: ProofPoint compliance embedded in SocialContentAppService
gapAnalysis.detail: ProofPoint compliance checks are invoked directly inside SocialContentAppService rather than as a domain policy or Specification. The invariant 'social content must pass compliance before scheduling' is invisible in the domain model and cannot be tested without the HTTP dependency. A CompliancePolicy specification should live in the domain layer.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events — side effects dispatched directly from AppService
gapAnalysis.detail: CreatePost, CreateChannel, CreateAnnouncement, and CreateComment all produce notifications by calling INotificationEventDispatcher directly from the AppService layer. ContentIngestedEvent and ContentUpdatedEvent are defined in the DataAccess/Infrastructure layers, not in Domain. The domain model has no event sourcing — all business-observable state changes are invisible to other aggregates without cross-service coupling.

gapAnalysis.title: Cross-aggregate compliance orchestration belongs in a domain service
gapAnalysis.detail: SocialComplianceAppService.CheckComplianceAsync orchestrates reads and writes across SocialShare, SocialContent, and UserComplianceDetails aggregates in a single method, then calls ProofPoint and DAS. This business decision logic (is this content compliant? can this user share?) is a domain service responsibility, not an application service responsibility. Moving it preserves invariants without coupling AppServices.

gapAnalysis.title: UMSEventConsumer bypasses aggregate lifecycle on user deactivation
gapAnalysis.detail: UMSEventConsumer directly calls service/repository methods for channel removal and social share cancellation without going through aggregate state transitions or raising domain events (UserDeactivated). This makes the deactivation side effects invisible to the domain model and untestable as invariants. A UserDeactivatedDomainEvent should trigger the affected aggregates.

gapAnalysis.title: AnnouncementPostEntity and AnnouncementSetting misnamed as entities
gapAnalysis.detail: AnnouncementPostEntity and AnnouncementSetting are used as value objects within AnnouncementEntity — they are replaced wholesale on update, not mutated in-place, and carry no identity. Their 'Entity' suffix causes DDD naming confusion. They should be renamed to AnnouncementPost and AnnouncementSchedule (value objects) to accurately reflect their role.

gapAnalysis.title: AIGeneratedPostEntity has no domain behavior
gapAnalysis.detail: AIGeneratedPostEntity is a pure data bag with no business methods, no lifecycle enforcement, and no invariants. All logic lives in AIGeneratedPostAppService which orchestrates external AI service calls. The domain object should at minimum encapsulate status transition rules (Pending → Generated → Failed) and cache invalidation invariants.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing domain events for successful state transitions
gapAnalysis.detail: ChannelEntity, PostEntity, CommentEntity, and AnnouncementEntity raise DomainException for invariant violations but emit no domain events for successful state transitions (e.g., ChannelRequestCreated, PostPublished, AnnouncementPublished). Domain events are needed to support eventual consistency, audit trails, and decoupled integration with the Notification domain — currently the app service directly calls the notification dispatcher, bypassing the domain event model.

gapAnalysis.title: Entitlement domain is a pure ACL adapter with no local model
gapAnalysis.detail: EntitlementController and EntitlementAppService are 1:1 pass-throughs to EntitlementServiceProvider. There is no cached role model, no local permission assertion, and no domain concept. This should be an infrastructure adapter (IEntitlementAdapter), not a named domain. Calling it a domain misleads future modelling and inflates the bounded context.

gapAnalysis.title: SocialStreamEntity conflates channel metadata with stream configuration
gapAnalysis.detail: SocialStreamEntity duplicates all ChannelEntity fields (ChannelId, ChannelType, ThumbnailId, PermissionEntity, RequestEntity, LastUserVisits) alongside stream-specific config (SocialNetworkSettings, ComplianceConfigurations, SearchParameters, RssFeeds, Interests). These are two concerns with separate change rates. The channel-level fields should be a reference (ChannelId FK), not a copy embedded in the stream aggregate.

gapAnalysis.title: UserAnnouncements acknowledgment produces no observable event
gapAnalysis.detail: UserAnnouncementsService.AcknowledgeAsync is a silent DB write with no domain event. This makes it impossible to trigger downstream effects (e.g. marking an announcement fully acknowledged when all channel members have read it, or surfacing analytics) without polling. An AnnouncementAcknowledged event is the missing concept.

gapAnalysis.title: NotificationEventDispatcher injected directly into AppServices
gapAnalysis.detail: INotificationEventDispatcher is injected into ChannelAppService, PostAppService, and others. Notification dispatch is an infrastructure side-effect that should be driven by domain events, not called directly in the application layer. This creates a tight coupling between business logic and notification infrastructure and makes AppServices harder to test.

gapAnalysis.title: PostEntity.Status is an untyped string
gapAnalysis.detail: PostEntity.Status is declared as string? with values like 'published' and 'draft' hardcoded as string literals across the codebase. This should be a PostStatus enum with a governed transition table inside the aggregate to prevent invalid lifecycle moves and catch errors at compile time.

gapAnalysis.title: Compliance value objects duplicated across Social Content and Social Share
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentResponse, Violation, Evidence, ContentCategory, ContentImage, ExtractedArticle are defined as identical inline mappings in both SocialContentEntity and SocialShareEntity constructors. These should be shared Value Objects in Domain/Common/ValueObjects so compliance data is modelled once and changes propagate consistently.

gapAnalysis.title: EntitlementAppService and FMSAppService are anemic pass-through facades
gapAnalysis.detail: Both services have zero domain logic and delegate 100% to their respective external providers. Introducing a controller+AppService layer for pure proxy concerns adds indirection without DDD value. These should be collapsed into Anti-Corruption Layer adapters injected directly where consumed, or absorbed into the domains that depend on them (Entitlement → Channel; FMS → Social Compliance).

gapAnalysis.title: UserDetailsAppService enforces domain invariants that belong in the aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: Stream-order deduplication, SocialNetworkPageType enum validation, and NetworkDefaultVisibility parsing all live in UserDetailsAppService.UpsertUserPreferenceDetailsAsync. These are invariants of the UserDetailsEntity aggregate and should be enforced inside it to prevent invalid state regardless of which AppService path is taken.

gapAnalysis.title: AIGeneratedPostEntity and GenerativeAISettingsEntity marked ExcludeFromCodeCoverage
gapAnalysis.detail: Both AI domain entities carry [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] attributes, indicating zero test coverage for the Generative AI domain. Combined with the absence of domain invariants in these entities, this domain has no safety net for behavioral regressions — high risk for a feature dependent on external AI service integration.

domains.name: Channel
operations: ChannelAppService: CreateChannelAsync, UpdateChannelAsync, GetChannelAsync, GetUserChannelsAsync, AddMemberAsync, RemoveMemberAsync, RequestAccessAsync, ApproveRequestAsync, VisitChannelAsync

invariants: A user cannot have two pending requests of the same AccessType for the same channel
A user already holding the requested permission level cannot re-submit a join request
ChannelType must be PUBLIC or PRIVATE
Member limit is capped at 200 per PermissionEntity

domains.name: Post
operations: PostAppService: CreatePostAsync, UpdatePostAsync, GetPostAsync, DeletePostAsync, GetPostsAsync, FeaturePostAsync, UnfeaturePostAsync

dddTarget.identity: PostId (conditionally set from request or generated externally)
invariants: Attachment ContentType must be one of LibraryContent, ProfileContent, WorkSpaceContent, PeerToPeerContent
LibraryContent attachment requires a LibraryContentExtension with TeamSiteId
ProfileContent attachment requires a ProfileContentExtension with ProfileVersionId
Attached content must resolve to a valid rendition in the external content store before the post is returned

domains.name: Comment & Reaction
operations: CommentAppService: CreateCommentAsync, GetCommentAsync, UpdateCommentAsync, DeleteCommentAsync, AddReactionAsync, RemoveReactionAsync

invariants: ContentType must be LibraryContent | ProfileContent | WorkSpaceContent | PeerToPeerContent

ProfileContent requires non-null ProfileContentExtension

operations: AnnouncementController: POST /announcements, GET /announcements, GET /announcements/{id}, PUT /announcements/{id}/post, PUT /announcements/{id}/settings, DELETE /announcements/{id}
AnnouncementAppService: CreateAnnouncementAsync, UpdateAnnouncementPostAsync, UpdateAnnouncementSettingsAsync, GetAnnouncementAsync, DeleteAnnouncementAsync
AnnouncementJobExecutor: background job fires at PublishDate for Scheduled announcements

invariants: PublishDate must be before ExpireDate for a non-draft announcement
Only users with seismic.channels.announcement.manage permission can create or update
PublishStatus is derived, never set directly

invariants: Content must complete VFS processing before video is playable

Ingested content triggers a Kafka event on eventbus.scp.content-management-application.ingested

SocialStreamAppService: CreateSocialStreamAsync, UpdateSocialStreamAsync, GetSocialStreamAsync, ListSocialStreamsAsync, DeleteSocialStreamAsync

RSS feed merge on update preserves UpContentCollectionId/Name from original when not provided in request

steps.label: POST /posts — post creation request with attachments
ChannelAppService: verify user is member of target channels
PostEntity: construct, validate attachment content types
ContentService (CMS): enrich attachment metadata
PostService: persist PostEntity to PostgreSQL
UserChannelsService: update channel LastPostTime
NotificationEventDispatcher: queue post-created notification
POST /announcements — create announcement request
EntitlementCheck: verify seismic.channels.announcement.manage permission
AnnouncementEntity: construct with computed PublishStatus
AnnouncementService: resolve recipient users from channel membership
AnnouncementService: persist to PostgreSQL
NotificationEventDispatcher: send immediate notification if status=Published
AnnouncementJobExecutor (Hangfire): fire at PublishDate for Scheduled announcements

workflows.name: Schedule Social Share with Compliance Check

steps.label: POST /social/shares — create social share request
SocialShareEntity: construct with delegate validation (mutual exclusivity check)
DASServiceProvider: fetch social compliance configuration
SocialComplianceAppService: evaluate compliance feature flag via FMS
ProofPoint: submit content for compliance evaluation
SocialShareEntity: update ComplianceStatus from ProofPoint result
SocialSharingServiceProvider: register share schedule externally
SocialShareService: persist to PostgreSQL

workflows.name: User Deactivation via UMS Kafka Event

steps.label: UMSEventConsumer: receive user.deactivated Avro Kafka event
UserChannelsService: remove user from all channel memberships
SocialShareService: cancel all pending social shares for user
UserComplianceDetailsEntity: delete social compliance record
SocialSharingServiceProvider: notify social sharing service of user deactivation
Direct DB calls bypass aggregate lifecycle — no domain events raised
